title: Halyard ingestion platform: quarantine surge across four tenants
domain: multi-tenant analytics event ingestion and warehouse loading
summary: Cairnmoor Data operates Halyard, a multi-tenant ingestion platform. Tenant edge-collector SDKs ship compressed event batches to an ingest-gateway, which decompresses and normalises the batch envelope. A contract-validator checks every record against the tenant's declared schema contract and diverts nonconforming records to a quarantine-store. A loader writes accepted records into the Meridian warehouse behind a per-shard circuit breaker. An hourly reconciliation job compares source and warehouse counts, a payload-integrity-check recomputes CRCs on large batches, and a canary gate screens transform deploys. Between 2026-09-08 and 2026-09-15 the platform ran a severity-2 incident. Determine what produced it and what should be done.

entities.name: Halyard
entities.note: Multi-tenant event ingestion and warehouse loading platform operated by Cairnmoor Data.

entities.name: edge-collector SDK
entities.note: Tenant-side library that batches, compresses and ships events; flushes a compression chunk every 8 MB.

entities.name: ingest-gateway
entities.note: Accepts tenant batches, decompresses them and normalises the batch envelope before validation.

entities.name: contract-validator
entities.note: Checks each record against the tenant's declared schema contract; diverts nonconforming records.

entities.name: quarantine-store
entities.note: Durable store holding records the contract-validator diverted, with a rate page attached.

entities.name: loader
entities.note: Writes accepted records into Meridian warehouse shards.

entities.name: loader circuit breaker
entities.note: Halts a shard's loads when its per-shard write-error rate crosses 2%, until manually released.

entities.name: reconciliation job
entities.note: Hourly comparison of a source-side record count against warehouse row counts per tenant.

entities.name: payload-integrity-check
entities.note: Recomputes a CRC against the tenant manifest for batches above a configured compressed-size threshold.

entities.name: canary gate
entities.note: Screens transform deploys against a held-out traffic slice before full promotion.

entities.name: Meridian warehouse
entities.note: Sharded analytic warehouse that is the destination for accepted records.

evidence.text: At 03:10 UTC on 2026-09-08 the Halyard on-call rotation received the first of 412 quarantine.rate.high pages. The fleet-wide contract-validator quarantine rate moved from a 30-day baseline of 0.02% to 6.1% and stayed there for the rest of the window.

Quarantine volume is concentrated in four tenants: Brightpath, Kestrel Logistics, Verdin Health and Tamarind Retail. Eleven other production tenants stayed inside their normal quarantine band throughout the window.

Brightpath's VP of Data filed SEV-2277, stating that the validator is destroying Brightpath reporting, and requesting that Brightpath traffic be exempted from contract validation until the reporting backlog clears.

Internal proposal RFC-441, written by the ingestion team and endorsed by two staff engineers, proposes a lenient validator mode that coerces nonconforming field values to their declared types and loads the record instead of diverting it.

The ingest-gateway fleet finished its staged rollout of release 4.12 at 03:04 UTC on 2026-09-08. The 4.12 changelog lists a decompression dependency upgrade and a logging change; it touches no schema-contract code and no loader code.
Brightpath upgraded its edge-collector SDK from 2.4.1 to 2.7.0 on 2026-09-05, three days before the first page. The 2.7.0 release notes list a change to batch flush behaviour.
Kestrel Logistics and Verdin Health both still run edge-collector 2.4.1 and are affected. Oakline Media runs edge-collector 2.7.0 and shows no quarantine increase at all.
A transform deploy, meridian-tx v88, reached full production at 14:00 UTC on 2026-09-09 after passing every canary-gate check on the held-out slice with no regression signal recorded.
Tenant-facing dashboard gaps were first reported by Kestrel Logistics at 06:30 UTC on 2026-09-08 and by Tamarind Retail at 09:15 UTC on 2026-09-08.

A sample of 500 quarantined records was summarised in the incident channel as type-coercion failures on the event_ts and payload_size fields. The on-call engineer recorded this as evidence of tenant-side schema drift.

Byte-level inspection of 60 quarantined records shows that every one of them is the last record of its batch, that each terminates mid-field with no closing delimiter, and that each is missing the trailing envelope checksum the collector appends.

Twelve batches that quarantined in production were replayed through a gateway instance pinned to release 4.11. All twelve validated cleanly and yielded exactly the record count declared in their batch manifests.

The edge-collector writes a separate gzip member for each 8 MB flush chunk, so any batch larger than 8 MB reaches the gateway as a multi-member gzip stream. Chunking is governed by tenant event volume and is identical in SDK 2.4.1 and 2.7.0.
Median compressed batch size over the window is 31 MB for Brightpath, 24 MB for Kestrel Logistics, 19 MB for Verdin Health, 27 MB for Tamarind Retail and 2 MB for Oakline Media.

The gateway's payload-integrity-check recomputes a CRC against the tenant manifest, but only for batches whose compressed size exceeds 64 MB. No batch in the incident window exceeded 64 MB, and the check emits no counter, log line or metric on the path where it does not run.

The hourly reconciliation job reported a 100.0% source-to-warehouse match for every tenant for every hour of the incident window, including all four affected tenants, and raised no reconciliation alert.

The reconciliation job reads its source-side count from the gateway counter records_accepted_post_normalization. The tenant-declared manifest total is carried in the batch envelope and is retained, but the job does not consult it.

Brightpath, Kestrel Logistics, Verdin Health and Tamarind Retail each independently compared their own manifest totals against Meridian row counts and report shortfalls of 9% to 13% for the window, roughly three orders of magnitude more records than the quarantine-store holds for them.

The loader circuit breaker tripped for six tenant shards between 02:00 and 04:40 UTC on 2026-09-10 when per-shard write-error rate crossed its 2% threshold, halting those shard loads until an engineer released them at 07:15 UTC.

The breaker's per-decision log is sampled at 1% and retained for 48 hours. The incident window's breaker decision records had already expired before the investigation opened, so what the halted shard loads would otherwise have committed cannot be determined from any retained source.

Two Meridian storage nodes reported elevated write latency between 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-12. The four tenants' shortfall rate is flat across the whole window and shows no step at those dates, and Meridian's durability audit for the window is clean.

A cost review filed the same week proposes cutting quarantine-store retention to a 1% sample, noting that quarantine storage grew roughly 300-fold in September and that the resulting pages are not telling the team anything the tenant dashboards do not already show.

The contract-validator's rule set has not changed since 2026-06-19. Its configuration hash is byte-identical at the start and at the end of the incident window, and no contract version bump is recorded for any affected tenant.

Sablefin Analytics runs batch volumes comparable to the four affected tenants. Sablefin's collector is configured not to transmit manifest totals, Sablefin has not run an independent row-count comparison, and Sablefin's contract is declared in permissive mode so no quarantine signal exists for it.
Halyard carries no end-to-end record-identity trace. Once a batch has been normalised there is no per-record lineage linking a warehouse row back to its ordinal position inside the source batch.

A platform-reliability ticket unrelated to the incident asks whether the loader breaker's 2% per-shard write-error threshold is too twitchy for shard-level noise and proposes 12% as a routine tuning change.

hypotheses.text: Brightpath's edge-collector 2.7.0 upgrade changed field serialisation so that records no longer satisfy the declared contract, driving the quarantine rate up.
Ingest-gateway 4.12 truncates multi-member compressed batches during envelope normalisation, malforming the tail record and discarding the remainder of the batch.
The meridian-tx v88 transform deploy changed the warehouse projection, so the tenant dashboard gaps reflect a presentation defect rather than an ingestion defect.
The contract-validator's rule set was tightened inside the incident window, so records that previously conformed now fail validation and are diverted to quarantine.
Meridian storage-node write latency caused loader batches to expire before commit, so records were acknowledged upstream but were never durably written to the warehouse.
Sablefin Analytics is losing records at the same rate as the four named tenants, and its own configuration is what prevents that loss from surfacing in any platform signal.

actions.text: Roll the ingest-gateway fleet back to release 4.11 and replay the affected batch range for the four tenants from their retained source archives.
Enable the lenient validator mode described in RFC-441 so that nonconforming field values are coerced to their declared types and the record is loaded.
Apply a contract-validation exemption to Brightpath traffic until the reporting backlog clears, then reinstate the contract for that tenant afterwards.
Raise the loader circuit breaker's per-shard write-error threshold from 2% to 12% so that shard loads stop halting on shard-level noise during the window.
Reduce quarantine-store retention to a 1% sample of diverted records and re-baseline the attached rate page against that new sampled volume.
Repoint the reconciliation job's source-side count at the tenant-declared manifest total carried in the batch envelope and re-run the job across the window.
Add a second validation stage that recomputes per-record checksums for every batch regardless of compressed size before any record is handed to the loader.
Restart the two Meridian storage nodes that reported elevated write latency and re-drive the six shard loads that the breaker halted on 2026-09-10.

controlPoints.text: The contract-validator together with the quarantine-store, considered over the incident window.
The ingest-gateway 4.12 envelope-normalisation step, considered over the incident window.
The loader's per-shard circuit breaker, considered over the incident window.
The gateway's payload-integrity-check, considered over the incident window.
The hourly reconciliation job as currently configured, considered over the incident window.
